bullets.title: The Death of Stalin
bullets.note:
(94% on Rotten Tomatoes)** This was brutally hilarious. The star performances from Steve Buscemi and others alone make it worth a watch, but the film is also broadly historically accurate. From the description: “The internal political landscape of 1950s Soviet Russia takes on darkly comic form in a film by Emmy Award-winning \[for [_Veep_](https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/veep)\] and Oscar-nominated \[for [_In the Loop_](https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/in_the_loop)\] writer/director [Armando Iannucci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armando_Iannucci).”  
​  
Check out the trailer [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E9eAshaPvYw) for a few laughs.

Buffalo for the Broken Heart: Restoring Life to a Black Hills Ranch
bullets.creator: Dan O’Brien)_
bullets.note: )_._ From the description: “For twenty years, Dan O’Brien struggled to make ends meet on his cattle ranch in South Dakota. But when a neighbor invited him to lend a hand at the annual buffalo roundup, O’Brien was inspired to convert his own ranch, the Broken Heart, to buffalo. Starting with thirteen calves, ‘short-necked, golden balls of wool,’ O’Brien embarked on a journey that returned buffalo to his land for the first time in more than a century and a half. _Buffalo for the Broken Heart_ is at once a tender account of the buffaloes’ first seasons on the ranch and an engaging lesson in wildlife ecology. … O’Brien combines a novelist’s eye for detail with a naturalist’s understanding to create an enriching, entertaining narrative.”
